text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Israeli air raids on Palestinian and Hizbollah targets in east and south Lebanon.
-Prime Minister Hariri, after meeting French President Chirac in Paris, said there would be no unilateral solution for Israeli occupation in south Lebanon.
-Lebanon's weekly treasury bill issue of February 6 raised 382.4 billion Lebanese pounds.
-Chirac said France would not send troops to south Lebanon if Israel withdrew unilaterally from its occupation zone.
-Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu said halting Hizbollah attacks against Israeli soldiers in south Lebanon is not a pre-condition for resuming peace talks with Syria.
-Middle East Airlines will complete a capital increase of $125 million on February 15.
-A U.S. security delegation will visit Beirut soon.
-State revenues from real estate taxes in 1996 reached 287.7 billion Lebanese pound.
-Top Israeli official visited the Israeli occupation zone in south Lebanon.
-Minister of Public Works Harajli said the rehabilitation of roads will cost $1.25 billion .
